extracted.intended_audience: general readers, reformers, and students of political economy interested in critiques of Malthusian theory (19th-century social criticism)
extracted.subtask_description: A 19th-century political-economy essay arguing against the Malthusian claim that population necessarily outstrips subsistence, using historical and contemporary examples (India, China, Ireland) to attribute famine and poverty to social, political, and economic causes rather than natural limits.
